judged.justification: Frames the historiographical starting point: Pico as neither Ficino's disciple nor a Savonarolan convert.

bears.note: Pico's historical model is said to differ even from Ficino's.
Poliziano's model is exclusive, unlike Ficino's and Pico's.
Barbaro's model of the historian of philosophy is compared with Pico's.

judged.justification: Separates Pico's and Ficino's inclusive approaches as two different models.

bears.note: Poliziano's Lamia is read as not aimed directly at Ficino and Pico.
Ficino and Pico are called Poliziano's friends holding different inclusive approaches.

judged.justification: Names Delmedigo as the formative influence on Pico's reading of Averroes on intellect and separate substances.
The book's verdict on Pico's use of Thomas.

quotes.t: Moving to theology, Chapters 14 and 15 contained discussions of the attacks of Pedro Garsia and Giovanni Caroli on Pico’s Apology, on some theses and on his approach to theology in general. Garsia criticizes what he regards as Pico’s Nominalist …

It is interesting, for instance, to find in Garsia a rather flexible understanding of the ‘common way’ which is determined according to the issue under examination and is not too dogmatic or schematic.
